page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors under the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 2 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on a shared allocation model running at a nominal base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, yielding a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The underlying AMD architecture includes 64 KB L1d cache, 512 KB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, and SHA_NI. No bundled local storage or integrated GPUs are included in this server configuration.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded processing capabilities offset by shared-resource constraints. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieves top-tier results, registering a score of 3622.88 in stress-ng and 2819.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside top-tier text processing throughput of 3466.0. However, multi-core metrics scale to average tiers, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 5010.0 and stress-ng multi-core scoring 7044.36. Memory-intensive benchmarks reveal lower performance boundaries; PassMark memory throughput registers in the bottom decile at 894.35, and cached small-block memory read bandwidth tests in the bottom 25% at 318.33 GB/sec. Large-block read and write bandwidth remain average at 49.26 GB/sec and 26.61 GB/sec, respectively.

In execution workloads, static web serving reaches an average throughput of 6.95 GB/sec, while in-memory operations show 3.74 million Redis SET operations per second. Lightweight machine learning inference with small 135M parameter models maintains average speeds of 539.4 prompt tokens per second, but falls to bottom-tier performance on medium 7B parameter models due to core count and memory bandwidth limits. The shared CPU topology yields cost-efficient entry-level compute for steady baseline execution, though multi-tenant contention may cause variability under extended heavy compute loads.

Given this hardware profile, UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is suited for low-to-moderate throughput web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, development environments, and single-thread-intensive batch processing where local persistent disk attachments are managed remotely.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is a cloud server configuration featuring 2 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor paired with 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, it delivers exceptional single-threaded performance, ranking in the top decile on Geekbench single-core and stress-ng tests. In contrast, multi-threaded output and memory subsystem bandwidth operate at average to lower-tier thresholds due to shared-core allocation and limited core density. The instance includes no onboard local storage and no hardware acceleration GPUs. It provides cost-effective utility for balanced, non-intensive general workloads such as light web hosting, API endpoints, microservices, and development pipelines that benefit from fast per-core instruction processing without heavy parallel concurrency demands.
